record.paper_title: Three Open Problems on the Wijsman Topology
record.original_question: Let (X, d) be a metric space. Let 2^X be the family of all non-empty closed subsets of X, and let T_W(d) be the Wijsman topology on 2^X; the Wijsman hyperspace of (X, d) is (2^X, T_W(d)). Without assuming that (X, d) is separable, is complete metrizability of (X, d) equivalent to some completeness-type topological property of the Wijsman hyperspace?

evidence.quote: Let $(X,d)$ be a metric space, and $2^X$ be the collection of all non-empty closed subsets of $X$.

The weakest topology on $2^X$ such that all functionals $d(\cdot, A)$, $A \in 2^X$, are continuous is called the \emph{Wijsman topology} and denoted by $\mathscr T_{W(d)}$. Correspondingly, we call $\left(2^X, \mathscr T_{W(d)}\right)$ the \emph{Wijsamn hyperspace} of $(X,d)$.
Problem 3.1. Is complete metrizability of (X, d) (without separability) equivalent to any completeness-type property of (2^X, T_W(d))?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,d)$ be a metric space, and let $2^X$ denote the family of all non-empty closed subsets of $X$. The Wijsman topology $\mathcal{T}_{W(d)}$ on $2^X$ is the weakest topology such that, for every $A \in 2^X$, the distance functional $d(\cdot, A): 2^X \to \mathbb{R}$ defined by $B \mapsto \inf\{d(b,a) : a \in A\}$ for $b \in B$ (taken as $\inf_{a\in A} d(b,a)$ evaluated pointwise, equivalently the functional $B \mapsto d(b,A)$ for each fixed $b \in X$ with the standard formulation $A \mapsto d(x,A)$, $x \in X$) is continuous. The pair $(2^X, \mathcal{T}_{W(d)})$ is called the Wijsman hyperspace of $(X,d)$.

Without assuming that $(X,d)$ is separable, determine whether there exists a completeness-type topological property $\mathcal{P}$ of the Wijsman hyperspace $(2^X, \mathcal{T}_{W(d)})$ such that $(X,d)$ is completely metrizable if and only if $(2^X, \mathcal{T}_{W(d)})$ has property $\mathcal{P}$.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem regarding non-separable metric spaces. Related results show that in the separable case complete metrizability of (X,d) is equivalent to complete metrizability of the Wijsman hyperspace, but for non-separable X there exists a complete metric space whose Wijsman hyperspace is not Čech-complete, and closed-hereditary completeness-type properties cannot characterize complete metrizability of X. No source found resolves the equivalence in general, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.snippet: There exists a non-separable complete metric space whose Wijsman hypertopology is not Čech-complete.
status_evidence.claim: Standard candidate completeness properties fail in the non-separable case, supporting that no easy answer is known.

status_evidence.title: Amsterdam properties of Wijsman hyperspaces
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses completeness-type (Amsterdam) properties of Wijsman hyperspaces.
status_evidence.claim: Related partial results exist but do not resolve the equivalence.
